sentiment.rationale: The document shows strong operational momentum with record revenues across all five businesses and positive operating leverage for the firm and each business. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to 'exceed $84 billion' from a prior expectation of $84 billion, and NII ex-Markets guidance was raised to 'up around 5.5%' from a prior expectation. However, expenses were guided higher than previously expected, and the CET1 capital ratio declined to 13.2% from 13.5% QoQ due to buybacks and RWA growth, partially offsetting the positive revenue momentum. The score reflects the genuine operational improvement and guidance raise, tempered by the expense headwind and capital decline.

summary.revenue: Total revenues of $22.1 billion in 3Q25, up 9% YoY. YTD 2025 revenues of $65.4 billion, up 7% YoY.
summary.eps: Diluted EPS of $1.86, up 23% YoY. Excluding the notable item (goodwill impairment), EPS was $2.24.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 revenues expected to exceed $84 billion. NII ex-Markets expected to be up around 5.5% for the full year. Expenses guided higher than the prior $53.4 billion target, excluding the goodwill impairment. Efficiency ratio expected to be slightly below 64% excluding the goodwill impairment. Targeting 10-11% RoTCE in 2026.
summary.margin: Efficiency ratio of 64.7% in 3Q25, improved 30 bps YoY. Excluding the notable item, the efficiency ratio was 61.4%, improved ~360 bps YoY. Net interest margin (NIM) was 2.40% in 3Q25, down 11 bps QoQ and up 7 bps YoY.
key_risks: Goodwill impairment of $726 million related to the Banamex transaction.
Corporate non-accrual loans increased 119% YoY to $2.1 billion, driven by idiosyncratic downgrades in Markets and Banking.
Consumer non-accrual loans increased 32% YoY to $1.6 billion, primarily driven by Wealth due to California wildfires.
CET1 Capital ratio declined to 13.2% from 13.5% QoQ, driven by common share repurchases, higher RWA, and dividends.
Expenses guided higher than previously expected for the full year.
Markets revenues expected to see a sequential decline from 3Q to 4Q that could exceed the historical range of 15-20%.
Uncertainty regarding the Federal Reserve's SCB averaging rule, leading to a higher CET1 target of 12.8%.
key_opportunities: Record revenues in all five businesses (Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth, USPB).
Positive operating leverage generated for the firm and each of the five businesses.
Record Net New Investment Assets in Wealth of $18.6 billion.
Continued momentum in Investment Banking with fees up 17% YoY and market share gains.
Strong growth in Services fee drivers: cross-border transactions up 10%, USD clearing volume up 5%, AUC/AUA up 13%.
Equity Markets prime balances up approximately 44% YoY.
New product launches in USPB (Citi Strata Elite card) and partnership with American Airlines.
Banamex 25% stake sale progressing towards full exit, with a path to deconsolidation and IPO.
Investments in AI and technology driving productivity and innovation.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Jane Fraser stated, 'The relentless execution of our strategy is delivering stronger business performance quarter after quarter and improving our returns,' and CFO Mark Mason said, 'We remain steadfast and focused on executing on our transformation, achieving our RoTCE target of 10 to 11% next year and further improving returns over time.'

evidence.claim: Total revenues were $22.1 billion in 3Q25, up 9% YoY.
evidence.quote: Citigroup revenues of $22.1 billion in the third quarter 2025 increased 9%, on a reported basis, driven by growth in each of Citi’s five interconnected businesses and Legacy Franchises, partially offset by a decline in Corporate/Other.

evidence.quote: Citigroup today reported net income for the third quarter 2025 of $3.8 billion, or $1.86 per diluted share, on revenues of $22.1 billion. This compares to net income of $3.2 billion, or $1.51 per diluted share, on revenues of $20.2 billion for the third quarter 2024.

evidence.claim: Expenses were guided higher than the prior $53.4 billion target.
